target_customer: Frontier tech companies (robotics, AI agents, drones, autonomy, hardware, space, defense) buying commercial insurance
problem: Standard commercial policies exclude or poorly cover autonomous systems, so frontier startups struggle to get proper coverage.
business_model: Insurance brokerage paid by insurers through commission on placed premium; founders pay nothing

founders.name: Samuel Gold
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; founders were already building insurance models.

competitors.name: RiskCube
competitors.what: Commercial coverage for AI, robotics, space and defense startups with fast certificates
competitors.funding_then: YC Fall 2024 company, amount not found

competitors.name: Valgo
competitors.what: Risk quantification platform for pricing physical AI risk

technical_complexity.rationale: A brokerage with AI drafted applications needs insurer relationships and licensing more than hard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Broker licensing and carrier partnerships help, but several funded AI brokerages target the same niche.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; incumbents were reported retreating from AI coverage.

market_need_then: Incumbent insurers add AI exclusions and robotics deployments are growing, leaving frontier firms without suitable cover.

identity.voice_and_tone: Thesis driven: 'Autonomy is being deployed faster than insurance has adapted to it.'

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press on the brand; the name resembles analytics style coinages like Riskalyze.

outcome_analysis: Risklytics is a two person Harvard leave team that launched in August 2026 as a brokerage for frontier tech insurance. No outcome exists yet. The need is plausible but the niche already has funded AI brokerages, and a commission model depends on carrier appetite for autonomy risk.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k Seed (single aggregator, unverified, not recorded as a round). Launch coverage labels it YC S26 while the directory says Fall 2026; dates may differ by source. Dealroom describes the business as catastrophe risk modeling, conflicting with the brokerage description. Competitors are dated to launch coverage in 2026, not older. Completeness pass: Round rests on a single database (Dealroom lists a $125k seed, no date or investors). Two searches found no press or filing.
